Gamma
[url=https://github.com/iqmanq/stardew-gamma#gamma][/url]
An AI assistant living inside Stardew Valley. Press a key in game and chat with an AI that can see your farm and search the Stardew Valley Wiki and the web to answer anything.
[quote]It knows your game, not just the wiki.[/quote][heading]Features[/heading]
[url=https://github.com/iqmanq/stardew-gamma#features][/url]
[b]Knows your game state[/b] — the AI gets a live snapshot and can pull details on demand:
[list]
[*]Your money, energy, health, skills, date, weather, daily luck and current location[/*]
[*]Everything in your backpack (stacks + item quality)[/*]
[*]Contents of every chest you own, per location (plus the farmhouse fridge)[/*]
[*]Active quests, objectives and progress (monsters slain, items delivered, days left)[/*]
[*]Friendship/heart levels with every villager, who you talked to/gifted today, birthdays[/*]
[*]Farm overview: buildings, animals (happiness, friendship), crops planted/ready to harvest, machines currently processing[/*]
[*]World progress: locations visited, unlocked areas, deepest mine/Skull Cavern level, Community Center completion, story events seen[/*]
[*]Every SMAPI mod you have installed (name, version, description) — so it knows if you're playing with SVE, Automation, etc.[/*]
[*]What's around you right now: NPCs in the area and their positions[/*]
[/list][b]Searches the outside world:[/b]
[list]
[*]Full Stardew Valley Wiki search + page reader (prices, schedules, gifts, bundles, mechanics…)[/*]
[*]General web search and web page reader (for modding help, news, anything else)[/*]
[/list][b]Extras:[/b]
[list]
[*]Multiple named chats, with history remembered per save across game sessions[/*]
[*]Replies, thinking indicators, tool progress, errors, and automatic titles stay with the chat where you sent the message, even while you switch chats or close the menu[/*]
[*]Independent requests in different chats can run at the same time[/*]
[*]Controller support in chat and settings, including free cursor movement and on-screen typing[/*]
[*]Unread-message badge on the HUD when it replies while the window is closed[/*]
[*]Console commands (see below) so you can use it without opening the UI[/*]
[/list]The mod never sends anything on its own — requests go out only when you send a message (chat window, or 
[code]gamma ask[/code] in the console).
[heading]Requirements[/heading]
[url=https://github.com/iqmanq/stardew-gamma#requirements][/url]
[list]
[*][url=https://smapi.io/]SMAPI[/url] 4.0+ (Stardew Valley 1.6)[/*]
[*]Access to an AI provider — a cloud API key, [b]or[/b] a free local model (see below)[/*]
[*]Optionally, a web-search API key (the wiki search works with no key at all)[/*]
[/list][heading]Setup[/heading]
[url=https://github.com/iqmanq/stardew-gamma#setup][/url]
[list=1]
[*]Install the mod: download 
[code]Gamma-1.0.1.zip[/code] from the [url=https://github.com/iqmanq/stardew-gamma/releases/latest]latest release[/url] (or from the Nexus page) and unzip it into your game's 
[code]Mods/[/code] folder — you should end up with 
[code]Mods/Gamma/[/code] containing 
[code]Gamma.dll[/code] and 
[code]manifest.json[/code]. (Alternatively, build from source — see [i]Building[/i] below; that installs into 
[code]Mods/[/code] automatically.)[/*]
[*]In game, press [b]O[/b] — if no API key is set yet, the [b]Gamma Settings[/b] screen opens automatically. Pick a provider (Google AI Studio, OpenRouter, OpenAI, Groq, Ollama, LM Studio, Anthropic…), paste your API key, and hit [b]Save[/b]. You can also get there any time via the [b]Settings[/b] button in the chat window or 
[code]gamma settings[/code] in the SMAPI console.[/*]
[*]If you prefer editing files by hand, run the game once so SMAPI creates 
[code]Mods/Gamma/config.json[/code], edit it, and restart.[/*]
[/list]Updating
[url=https://github.com/iqmanq/stardew-gamma#updating][/url]
Close the game, download the latest release ZIP, and replace 
[code]Gamma.dll[/code] and 
[code]manifest.json[/code] in your existing 
[code]Mods/Gamma/[/code] folder. Keep your 
[code]config.json[/code] to preserve provider settings and API keys; chat history is stored separately by SMAPI. Restart the game to load the update. See [url=https://github.com/iqmanq/stardew-gamma/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md]CHANGELOG.md[/url] for release changes.
Getting an API key
[url=https://github.com/iqmanq/stardew-gamma#getting-an-api-key][/url]
Gamma needs one API key from any supported provider. Two good free options:
[b]Option 1 — Google AI Studio (free, recommended)[/b]
[list=1]
[*]Go to [url=https://aistudio.google.com/]aistudio.google.com[/url] and sign in with a Google account.[/*]
[*]Click [b]Get API key[/b] in the sidebar (or open [url=https://aistudio.google.com/apikey]aistudio.google.com/apikey[/url] directly).[/*]
[*]Click [b]Create API key[/b], choose or create a project, and copy the key (starts with 
[code]AIza[/code]).[/*]
[*]In Gamma's settings screen (press [b]O[/b] in game), pick the [b]Google AI Studio[/b] preset, paste the key, and hit [b]Save[/b]. The model is pre-filled to 
[code]gemini-flash-lite-latest[/code].[/*]
[/list]Recommended model: 
[code]gemini-flash-lite-latest[/code] — fast, 500 free requests per day, and good enough at tool-calling for everyday questions. If you want stronger reasoning for harder questions, 
[code]gemini-flash-latest[/code] or 
[code]gemini-3.5-flash[/code] (requires setting up billing, paid) are drop-in upgrades (same key, just change the Model field).
[b]Option 2 — OpenRouter (free tier available)[/b]
[list=1]
[*]Go to [url=https://openrouter.ai/]openrouter.ai[/url] and sign up (email or Google/GitHub login).[/*]
[*]Open [url=https://openrouter.ai/settings/keys]openrouter.ai/settings/keys[/url] (Profile → [b]Keys[/b]).[/*]
[*]Click [b]Create key[/b], give it any name, and copy it (starts with 
[code]sk-or-v1-[/code], shown only once — save it somewhere).[/*]
[*]Free models work out of the box; there's no need to add credits unless you pick paid models.[/*]
[*]In Gamma's settings screen, pick the [b]OpenRouter[/b] preset, paste the key, and hit [b]Save[/b]. The model is pre-filled to 
[code]openrouter/free[/code].[/*]
[/list]Recommended model: 
[code]openrouter/free[/code] — OpenRouter's free-model router, which automatically selects an available free model. Free models have daily limits and can be busy at peak times; if a request fails with a rate-limit error, try again later or choose a specific model from the provider's model list.
[b]Manual setup[/b] — if you'd rather edit the config file than use the in-game screen, run the game once so SMAPI creates 
[code]Mods/Gamma/config.json[/code], then set 
[code]Provider[/code], 
[code]ApiKey[/code], and 
[code]Model[/code] as in the examples below and restart.
AI provider examples
[url=https://github.com/iqmanq/stardew-gamma#ai-provider-examples][/url]
[b]OpenAI[/b]
{
  "Provider": "openai",
  "ApiKey": "sk-...",
  "Model": "gpt-4o-mini"
}

[b]Google AI Studio[/b] (free key — see [i]Getting an API key[/i] above)
{
  "Provider": "openai",
  "ApiBaseUrl": "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/",
  "ApiKey": "AIza...",
  "Model": "gemini-flash-lite-latest"
}

[b]Anthropic (Claude)[/b]
{
  "Provider": "anthropic",
  "ApiKey": "sk-ant-...",
  "Model": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
}

[b]OpenRouter / Groq / DeepSeek / etc.[/b] (any OpenAI-compatible API)
{
  "Provider": "openai",
  "ApiBaseUrl": "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1",
  "ApiKey": "sk-or-...",
  "Model": "openrouter/free"
}

[b]100% free & local with Ollama[/b] (no API key, no internet)
ollama pull llama3.1:8b

{
  "Provider": "openai",
  "ApiBaseUrl": "http://localhost:11434/v1",
  "ApiKey": "ollama",
  "Model": "llama3.1:8b"
}

LM Studio works the same way with 
[code]http://localhost:1234/v1[/code]. Local models are slower and weaker at tool-calling than cloud models — a mid-size instruct model or larger recommended.
Web search (optional)
[url=https://github.com/iqmanq/stardew-gamma#web-search-optional][/url]
The wiki search always works with zero setup. For general web search, set one of:
{
  "SearchProvider": "tavily",      // free tier at tavily.com
  "SearchApiKey": "tvly-..."
}

or 
[code]"SearchProvider": "brave"[/code] (brave.com/search/api) or 
[code]"SearchProvider": "searxng"[/code] with 
[code]"SearxngUrl": "http://localhost:8080"[/code] for a self-hosted instance (no key needed). SearXNG disables its JSON API by default; enable it in the instance's 
[code]settings.yml[/code]:
search:
  formats:
    - html
    - json

then restart the instance, or the mod will report "refused the JSON API". In the in-game settings, pick 
[code]searxng[/code] and the search row becomes the instance URL field.
[heading]Usage[/heading]
[url=https://github.com/iqmanq/stardew-gamma#usage][/url]
[list]
[*][b]O[/b] (configurable via 
[code]OpenChatKey[/code]) opens the chat window. Enter sends, Esc closes, scroll wheel reviews history.[/*]
[*][b]Controller[/b]: clicking the [b]right stick[/b] (configurable via 
[code]OpenChatGamepadButton[/code]) also opens the chat window. Inside it, the game's usual gamepad support applies — left stick freely moves the cursor even with snappy menus enabled, [b]A[/b] clicks (and opens the keyboard only when pressed over a text field), right stick scrolls, [b]X[/b] starts a new chat, [b]LB/RB[/b] (or triggers) switch chats, [b]D-pad up/down[/b] scrolls history, and [b]B[/b] closes the keyboard, then clears the input, then closes the window. OSK [b]Start[/b] submits the message. [b]Y[/b] does nothing in either menu. In settings, [b]A[/b] on a text field opens the keyboard, [b]LB/RB[/b] (or triggers / D-pad up/down) cycle all fields and buttons, [b]X[/b] saves, [b]B[/b] cancels. Navigation includes provider/auth options, [b]Load list[/b], [b]Web search[/b], [b]Name chats with AI[/b], and Save/Cancel. Hovering or selecting a field with LB/RB does not open the keyboard.[/*]
[*]When a reply arrives while the window is closed, a badge appears on the HUD.[/*]
[*][b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b] — if you have [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]GMCM[/url] installed, every option (provider, key, model, web search, the chat keybinds, and the chatbot's display name) is editable in its UI at the title screen or under the game's options cog icon. "Reset to defaults" there deliberately keeps your API keys.[/*]
[*]SMAPI console commands:
[list]
[*][code]gamma menu[/code] — open the chat window[/*]
[*][code]gamma ask <text>[/code] — ask without the UI (reply is printed to the console)[/*]
[*][code]gamma wiki <query>[/code] — quick wiki search[/*]
[*][code]gamma state[/code] — dump the same state summary the AI sees[/*]
[*][code]gamma mods[/code] — list installed mods[/*]
[*][code]gamma reset[/code] — clear chat history[/*]
[/list][/*]
[/list][heading]Privacy[/heading]
[url=https://github.com/iqmanq/stardew-gamma#privacy][/url]
When you send a message, the mod sends a summary of your game state (the "snapshot" plus whatever tools the AI chooses to call — inventory, chests, quests, mod list…) to the AI provider you configured. Nothing is sent until you ask something. Use a local model via Ollama/LM Studio if you want everything to stay on your machine.
[heading]Building[/heading]
[url=https://github.com/iqmanq/stardew-gamma#building][/url]
Requires the .NET SDK (any recent version) and Stardew Valley 1.6 + SMAPI installed.
cd Gamma
dotnet build

The build compiles against your local game DLLs and copies 
[code]Gamma.dll[/code] + 
[code]manifest.json[/code] into 
[code]Mods/Gamma/[/code] automatically. If the game isn't in the default Steam location, point at it:
dotnet build -p:GamePath="C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Stardew Valley"

[heading]Troubleshooting[/heading]
[url=https://github.com/iqmanq/stardew-gamma#troubleshooting][/url]
[list]
[*][i]"I'm not set up yet"[/i] — the config has no working provider. Fill 
[code]ApiKey[/code] (or 
[code]ApiBaseUrl[/code] for local), then restart the game.[/*]
[*][b]API key errors[/b] — check the key and that 
[code]Model[/code] matches the provider's model names.[/*]
[*][b]Web search says it's not configured[/b] — set 
[code]SearchProvider[/code] + 
[code]SearchApiKey[/code].[/*]
[*]Anything else — check the SMAPI console/log (
[code]ErrorLogs/SMAPI-latest.txt[/code]) for 
[code][Gamma][/code] lines.[/*]
[/list][heading]Testing[/heading]
[url=https://github.com/iqmanq/stardew-gamma#testing][/url]
Run the conversation-routing regression checks with the .NET 8 SDK:
dotnet run --project tests/ConversationRouting.csproj

These use a fake provider and game stubs to check chat switching, concurrent requests, progress/reply/error/title ownership, persistence, and late replies after deletion or loading another save. They do not make network requests or touch real saved chats.
The in-game UI harness exercises real game controls and rendering:
[list]
[*][b]In game[/b]: run 
[code]gamma testui[/code] in the SMAPI console. It seeds a sample conversation, opens the chat window, sends one real chat request, checks A/Y/B keyboard behavior, opens the settings screen, and saves a screenshot of each step to 
[code]Mods/Gamma/ui-tests/[/code].[/*]
[*][b]Fully headless[/b] (no window, no audio, quits when done):
./run-headless-test.sh                      # uses your configured model
GAMMA_AUTO_TEST_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini ./run-headless-test.sh

This launches the real game under a virtual display with all audio muted (SDL dummy driver + OpenAL null backend), runs the same automated pass, and writes the log and screenshots out. Note: headless runs render at a slightly different scale than a real window, so use the screenshots to check content/colors, not exact pixel layout. Use a test history: the harness clears the current chat and adds test conversations. Physical controller movement still needs an in-game check.[/*]
[/list][heading]How it works (for the curious)[/heading]
[url=https://github.com/iqmanq/stardew-gamma#how-it-works-for-the-curious][/url]
The mod is a state bridge: SMAPI events and the game API (
[code]Game1.*[/code]) are read into compact text summaries; the AI gets the summaries as context and a set of ~13 tools (
[code]get_chests[/code], 
[code]search_wiki[/code], 
[code]web_search[/code], …) implemented as a read-only tool-calling loop against either an OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic endpoint. Tool bodies are marshalled onto the game thread so reads never race the game's tick loop. The UI reuses the vanilla menu box texture, chat text field, fonts and sounds.
